subtopics.title: Milano Cortina 2026 Edition
subtopics.summary: The 25th Winter Olympic Games were held from 6 to 22 February 2026 in Italy, with Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo as joint hosts. It was the first joint two-city Winter Olympics and Italy's fourth time hosting an Olympic Games. The Opening Ceremony was at the San Siro Stadium in Milan and the Closing Ceremony at the Verona Arena.
facts: 25th Winter Olympic Games held 6-22 February 2026
Hosts: Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy
First joint two-city Winter Olympics
Italy's fourth time hosting an Olympic Games
Earlier Italian hosting: Cortina 1956 (Winter), Rome 1960 (Summer), Turin 2006 (Winter)
Opening Ceremony: San Siro Stadium, Milan
Closing Ceremony: Verona Arena
Official motto: 'IT's Your Vibe'
Mascots: Tina and Milo (white stoats)
Theme 'Armonia' (Harmony); 16 winter sports, debut sport Ski Mountaineering (Skimo)

subtopics.title: Medal Tally and Participation
subtopics.summary: Norway topped the final medal table for the fourth consecutive time, with 41 medals including 18 gold. The USA (33 medals, 12 gold) and the Netherlands (20 medals, 10 gold) followed, and host Italy won 30 medals. India sent two athletes, who won no medals, and Abhinav Bindra was India's torchbearer.
facts: Norway: 41 medals, 18 gold; topped the final table
Norway topped the final medal table for the 4th consecutive time
USA: 33 medals, 12 gold
Netherlands: 20 medals, 10 gold
Italy: 30 medals (10 gold, 6 silver, 14 bronze)
India fielded 2 athletes and won no medals
Arif Mohammad Khan: Alpine Skiing, Men's Slalom
Stanzin Lunduo: Cross-Country Skiing
India's torchbearer: Abhinav Bindra, India's 1st individual Olympic gold medallist

subtopics.title: History of the Olympic Games
subtopics.summary: The ancient Olympic Games started in 776 BCE at Olympia, Greece, and the record of the last ancient Games is found in 261 AD. Baron Pierre de Coubertin founded the modern Olympics, and the first modern international event was held at Athens in 1896. Women first took part at the 1900 Paris Olympics, the same year India first participated.
facts: Ancient Olympic Games started in 776 BCE at Olympia, Greece
In 393 AD, Theodosius I banned the Olympics along with Greek temples and god statues
Record of the last ancient Olympic Games found in 261 AD
Founder of the modern Olympics: Baron Pierre de Coubertin

Women first took part at the 1900 Paris Olympics; Margaret Abbott (Golf) became the first female Olympic champion
2020 Olympics postponed to 2021 due to COVID-19 restrictions
Olympics cancelled due to WWI: Berlin (1916)
India first participated in 1900, first sent a Summer team in 1920, and competed at Innsbruck (Austria) Winter Games in 1964
Norman Pritchard, a lone athlete, won 2 silver medals in athletics

subtopics.title: Olympic Bodies and India's Sports Schemes
subtopics.summary: The International Olympic Committee, established in 1894, is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, and its President is Kirsty Coventry. In India, the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports is the nodal ministry, supported by schemes such as TOPS (2014), Khelo India (2017), Fit India (2019) and KIRTI (2024). A WADA 2023 report placed India high on banned-substance positivity among major nations.
facts: IOC: established 1894, headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland
IOC President: Kirsty Coventry
IOC motto: Citius, Altius, Fortius (Faster, Higher, Stronger)
Indian Olympic Association: set up 1927, President PT Usha, HQ New Delhi
Nodal ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports
TOPS (2014): identifies and supports athletes with potential to win Olympic medals
Khelo India (2017): identification and development of athletes at grassroots and elite levels
Fit India Movement (2019): mass participation in fitness activities
KIRTI Programme (2024): talent hunt among school children aged 9 to 18
WADA 2023 report: India had the highest positivity rate for banned substances among major nations

quizzes.passage:
The Olympic Games have a history that begins in ancient Greece, where the early Games were held at Olympia. Records of the last ancient Games are found in the history books, which shows that the tradition lasted for a long time before it came to an end.

The ancient Games were later brought to an end by an order that also targeted Greek temples and statues of gods. The ban was part of an effort to promote Christianity across the empire.

The modern Olympic movement took shape in the late nineteenth century. A founder led its revival, and an international committee was set up to organise the movement. The first modern international event was held in a Greek city, after a royal announcement that the Games would begin again.

The modern movement is now governed by an international body based in Switzerland. Over the years, the Olympics have had to adapt to changing times, and some editions were disrupted by global conflicts. India first took part in the Olympics in an early edition, and it first sent a team to the Summer Games at a later date. Indian athletes have also competed at a Winter Games held in Austria. Italy has hosted the Olympic Games on several occasions, including the Winter Games in Cortina in 1956, and Rome hosted the Summer Games in 1960.
